summary.text: Dan Osborn is an industrial mechanic and union leader from Omaha running as an independent (ballot line "Nonpartisan") for the second consecutive Senate cycle. A Navy and Nebraska Army National Guard veteran, he lost to Sen. Deb Fischer in 2024. His campaign centers on congressional ethics reform, consumer-protection and antitrust measures, and opposition to cuts in Social Security and Medicare.

paragraphs.text: Osborn lives in Omaha, Nebraska. He served in the U.S. Navy and the Nebraska Army National Guard, and his campaign website says he handled inventory on the USS Constellation.
He worked as an industrial mechanic at Kellogg's plant in Omaha, where he was president of a local chapter of the Bakery, Confectionery, Tobacco Workers and Grain Millers International Union.
Osborn first ran for the U.S. Senate in 2024 as a nonpartisan candidate and lost to incumbent Sen. Deb Fischer (R), 53.2% to 46.5%.
In 2026 he is again running without a party label, this time against Sen. Pete Ricketts. The Nebraska Democratic Party endorsed him, and he has said he will not caucus with either party if elected.
